 Judgment
The Police Sub-Inspector of R.T.Nagara Police Station submitted charge sheet against accused for the offences punishable under Section 498(A), 341, 506 of Indian Penal Code.
2. Prosecution Case:
The marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Mustaqueem was solemnized with accused in the year 2003 and from the said marriage, they have 2 children.
Thereafter the accused started to harass CW1 and subjected her to physical and mental cruelty and hence she left the accused and started residing separately.

That being so, on 12-06- 2022 at about 10.45 p.m. the CW1 along with her son KABC030589312022 CC No.23267/2022 CW2 Sri Mohammed Oves were going on their two wheeler on 5th Cross of Dinnur within the limits of R. T. Nagara PS, the accused wrongfully restrained them and abused with filthiest language and thereby committed the aforesaid offences.

3. First Information Report: On the basis of first information given by informant cum CW1 namely Smt.Mustaqueem, Smt. Choodamani, ASI of R.T.Nagara police registered a Crime No.167/2022 against the accused for the offenses punishable under Section 498(A), 341, 504 of IPC, prepared FIR and sent the same to the Court and to his superior officers.
4. Investigation:
After registration of crime No. 167/2022, the CW7 has handed over the case papers to CW8.
On the receipt of case papers, CW8 drawn the spot mahazar as per Ex. P. 2 and secured the marriage photographs and marriage invitation card and recorded the statement of witnesses.
After completion of investigation, the I.O/CW8 has filed charge sheet against accused.
5. On receipt of charge sheet, this Court took cognizance of offences alleged against the accused.
KABC030589312022 CC No.23267/2022 6. Thereafter the accused filed application and obtained bail.
7. Copies of prosecution paper as required U/Sec.207 of Cr.P.C have been furnished to the accused.

8. Charges: After hearing learned Sr.APP and counsel for accused, charge for the offences punishable U/Sec.498(A), 341, 504 of Indian Penal Code has been framed, read over and explained to the accused in the language known to him, who, in turn, pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
9. Prosecution Evidence:
The prosecution in order to establish its case cited 8 witnesses, examined one witness and exhibited 3 documents.

The learned Sr.APP has prayed for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses however his prayer was rejected on the ground that no purpose would be served as the material witness -PW1 has not supported the case by the order dated 11-09-2024.

10. Accused statement as per section 313 of CrPC: There are no incriminating evidences against the accused from the evidence of prosecution thereby the recording of statement of accused as per Sec.313 of Cr.P.C. is dispensed with.

sentences.text: Heard the arguments.
Perused materials on the record.

12. The following point are arises for consideration is as follows;
1.

Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that The marriage of CW1 namely Smt. Mustaqueem was solemnized with accused in the year 2003 and from the said marriage, they have 2 children.

Thereafter the accused started to harass CW1 and subjected her to physical and mental cruelty and hence she left the accused and started residing separately thereby resulted in commission of the offences punishable U/sec.498(A) of IPC?

2. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that on 12-06-2022 at about 10.45 p.m. the CW1 along with her son CW2 Sri KABC030589312022 CC No.23267/2022 Mohammed Oves were going on their two wheeler on 5th Cross of Dinnur within the limits of R. T. Nagara PS,
the accused wrongfully restrained them thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.
341 of IPC?

3. Whether the prosecution proved beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused abused CW1 and 2 with filthiest language intentionally insulted them knowingly such insult will provoke breach of peace thereby resulted in commission of an offence punishable u/Sec.
504 of IPC?
4. What order?

13. My findings on the above points are as under:
 Point No.1 to 3 : In the Negative  Point No. 4 : As per final order  KABC030589312022 CC No.23267/2022  REASONS 14.
Point No.1 & 2:
These points are taken up together for the purpose of common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts as they form the same part of transaction.

In support of Rt Nagar Police Station vs Zabiulla on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133301134/
3 prosecution case as narrated in paragraph 2 and the point for consideration in paragraph 12 of this judgment, the prosecution has examined the witness, as follows i.

sentences.text: CW1 by name Smt.Mustaqueem
- Informant examined as PW1 deposed that she has identified her signatures on Ex.P1 -complaint and Ex.P2 -spot mahazar.

When she went to police station for settlement of minor grievances between her and accused, the police obtained her signatures on the said documents and she pleaded ignorance about the contents of complaint.
In this regard, the learned Sr.APP has cross examined this witness by treating her as hostile witness but no favorable answer has been elicited from her mouth to support the prosecution case.

Her denial of statement given before the police is marked as Ex.P3.
15.
In the present case, the learned APP prays for issuance of summons to other witness.
It is seen from the entire records that, PW.1 is the material witnesses to the prosecution case however she did not support the prosecution case in any manner.
Under these circumstances, this court is of the opinion that, even if other witness examined by the prosecution and they supported the prosecution that would not helpful to the case of prosecution.
At this background, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of Court in examining other witness.
Moreover the evidence of other witnesses is only formal in nature.

Therefore, the prayer of learned APP is rejected and the prosecution evidence is taken as closed by the order dated 11/09/2024.
16.
It is seen from record that PW1 and accused obtained divorce in OS No.297/2024 by mutual consent wherein she has undertaken to withdraw all cases pending between them.

But the learned APP argued that the Section 498A R/w Section 34 of Indian Penal code is not compoundable case as per section 320 of CRPC and hence the examination of all the witnesses is necessary but this court dispensed the same on account of amicable settlement arrived between the rival parties to the case.
Yes this court agrees with the view of the Learned APP that the section 498A of IPC is not compoundable and the same cannot be compounded as per Section 320 of CRPC.

This court places reliance in the case of B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. STATE OF HARYANA AND ANR IN THE MATTER OF AIR 2003 SCW 1824, wherein it was held that, KABC030589312022 CC No.23267/2022 "in a case where matrimonial disputes have been resolved between the parties then in that case offence under Section 498A of I.P.C. may be compounded between the parties for according to them an opportunity to settle in life afresh.

entities.text: B.S. JOSHI AND ORS. V. STATE OF HARYANA AND ANR
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
17. This court further places reliance upon the decision in the case of Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat), wherein this lordship observed which runs thus:
"It appears that good sense have been prevailed amongst the spouses and when it became impossible for them to lead conjugal life any further and when the matrimonial home has been broken for all practical purposes, they have decided to withdraw all allegations and counter allegations against each other and get themselves separated on divorce by mutual consent.

entities.text: Ranjana Banerjee v. Bijay Bhushan Banerjee and Ors., 1996(2) East. Cri. C. 808 (Pat)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Although, Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code is not compoundable, but in the nature and circumstances of the Rt Nagar Police Station vs Zabiulla on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/133301134/
4 case and the situation prevailing, accord is hereby granted to compromise the dispute between the parties and hence joint petition filed in both the cases are hereby allowed."

sentences.text:
It further held that after examining the KABC030589312022 CC No.23267/2022 nature of the case and the circumstances, under which the offence has been committed, it would be proper to compound the offence and in my opinion, it would be also meet the ends of justice."
18. ADMITTEDLY, the disputes between the PW1 and accused have been resolved.
The criminal case under Section 498A of I.P.C. is the off-shoot of the said matrimonial dispute.
The parties have come to their terms and in pursuance thereto the CW1/Pw1 does not intend to proceed with this case and hence she has not supported the prosecution case.

19. In the case of KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464, wherein it was held that "it would be unfair or contrary to the interest of justice to continue with the criminal proceeding or continuation of criminal proceeding would tantamount to abuse of process of law despite settlement and compromise between the victim and the wrongdoer and whether to secure the ends of justice, it is appropriate that criminal case is put to an end".
20.

entities.text: KRISHNA vs STATE OF KARNATAKA reported in Laws(Kar) 2014 4 464
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Under these circumstances and on account of the preposition laid down by the Hon'ble Apex and Hon'ble High Court, even if other witnesses examined by the prosecution, they did supported the prosecution, would not helpful to the prosecution.
In KABC030589312022 CC No.23267/2022 this background, this court feels it is a waste of precious time of the Court in examining other witnesses.
Moreover the evidence of other witnesses is only formal in nature.

Therefore, the prayer of learned APP is rejected and prosecution evidence is taken as closed and hence the offence under section 498A of IPC with other offences under section 341, 506 of IPC cannot be proved beyond reasonable doubt.
Accordingly, this court answers the point No.1 to 3 in the Negative.
21. Point No.3:-

In view of the above findings and reasons given on point No.1 to 3, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER Acting U/Sec.248(1) of the Cr.P.C.
(i) The accused is found not guilty and acquitted from the offences punishable under Sec.498(A), 341, 504 of IPC.
(ii) Accused is set at liberty.
(iii) In view of Section 437-A of Cr.P.C his bail bond shall be in force for 6 (six)
months.

KABC030589312022 CC No.23267/2022 (iv) Ordered accordingly.
